concepts.title: The Four Factors of Production
concepts.definition: Production needs four classic inputs - land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship - classified as factors of production; businesses combine them, paying rent for land, wages for labour and interest for capital, while profit rewards the organiser who bears the risk.
concepts.key_idea: Land, labour, capital and enterprise join to produce; each factor earns its own return.
question_patterns: name the four factors of production
what does each factor of production earn as a reward
why are land, labour and capital not enough without enterprise
give one example of each factor of production from a bakery
define factors of production in your own words
which factor of production organises the other three

solution_steps.explain: Identify land, labour, capital and the organising entrepreneur in any production story.
Rent, wages, interest and profit respectively pay for the four factors.
Production happens only when all four factors work together.

concepts.title: Land as a Factor: Natural Resources
concepts.definition: In economics, land means far more than ground - it covers all natural gifts like soil, forests, water, air and minerals that businesses use, paying rent for them; the gifts of nature set the base on which production stands.
concepts.key_idea: Land in economics is every free gift of nature used in production.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees107.txt lines 160-175 (land encompasses natural resources, rent)
question_patterns: what does the term land include in economics
why are minerals and forests counted under land
what reward does the factor land receive
how does the quality of land affect production
give examples of land as a factor of production
can the supply of land be increased - explain

solution_steps.explain: Include soil, water, forests, air and minerals as land.
Nature's total supply of these gifts cannot be expanded at will.
Users pay rent for the right to employ these natural inputs.

concepts.title: Labour and Human Effort
concepts.definition: Labour is the physical and mental human effort that turns materials into goods and services - from a farmer's fieldwork to an engineer's design - and it earns wages; the quality of labour, shaped by education and skill, decides how productive an economy can be.
concepts.key_idea: Every productive human effort, bodily or mental, is labour paid as wages.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees107.txt lines 175-230 (labour as a factor, wages)
question_patterns: define labour as a factor of production
what reward does labour receive
distinguish physical and mental labour with examples
how does education improve the quality of labour
why is labour called an active factor of production
give two examples of skilled labour in your area

solution_steps.explain: Count all human work - manual and intellectual - applied to production.
Training and education raise labour productivity.
Wages and salaries are the returns to labour.

concepts.title: Capital and Entrepreneurship
concepts.definition: Capital means the man-made aids of production - machines, tools, buildings, money invested - earning interest, while the entrepreneur supplies ideas, organises the other factors, takes risks and earns profit; technology acts as an enabler that multiplies what all four factors can produce.
concepts.key_idea: Machines and money are capital; the risk-taking organiser is the entrepreneur, rewarded by profit.
question_patterns: define capital with examples
what is the reward for capital
what functions does an entrepreneur perform
why does the entrepreneur earn profit
how does technology act as an enabler of production
distinguish capital from land as factors of production

solution_steps.explain: Machines, tools and invested money count as capital earning interest.
The entrepreneur combines factors, innovates and bears losses.
Better technology raises the output of the same land, labour and capital.
